title: Game Instructions
introduction: The complete Kaiser XI manual, from creating a League through troubleshooting.
details: How it works

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.overview: Kaiser XI turns real football performances into a private fantasy competition whose format and rules are chosen by your group.
details: In Kaiser XI, real football players are assigned to Fantasy Teams. For every Matchday, the recorded base rating and match events produce each player’s fantasy score; the eligible players in a submitted formation then produce the Fantasy Team score. That score is used differently in Classic Championship, Head-to-Head, and Formula One leagues.

Register with your name, email address, and password, then sign in. The dashboard is the starting point for leagues and invitations; authentication is only the doorway, while all competition work happens inside a league.

To create a league, choose Create League and complete the setup. You become its Commissioner: you invite managers, maintain membership and rules, record initial squads, initialize the competition, configure the Market, and calculate completed Matchdays.

To join, open a valid invitation link while signed in and accept it. You enter the inviter’s league as a member under that Commissioner’s configuration; accepting does not make you Commissioner, and the participant limit must not already be full.

After joining, check whether a Fantasy Team has been assigned to you. Your League Rules determine budgets, roster limits, formations, substitutions, scoring, Market windows, and trades, so read them before selecting a lineup.

Your League. Your Rules. means that Kaiser XI supplies the competition framework while each league’s saved settings decide how that group plays. The general manual explains the controls; the League Rules page is authoritative for your particular league.
gettingStarted.callout: Begin by opening the dashboard, then either create one league or accept the invitation supplied by its Commissioner.

creatingLeague.title: Creating a League
creatingLeague.overview: League creation links one private fantasy league to one real competition Season and establishes its identity, format, capacity, and starting roster rules.
details: Enter a required League name (up to 255 characters) and, optionally, a description (up to 5,000 characters). Use the description for group context, not for rules that should be enforced: enforceable rules belong in League Rules.

Select one of the Seasons actually listed in the form. Each entry shows its real competition and Season. This choice fixes the Matchdays, real matches, registered players, roles, and PlayerScores available to the league; it is therefore much more than a display label. Kaiser XI only offers Seasons already configured in the application.

Choose the League type. In Classic Championship, teams are ranked by the cumulative fantasy points from calculated championship Matchdays: for example, scores of 72 and 68 give 140 total. In Head-to-Head, generated fixtures pair teams; default thresholds convert 65 points to 0 goals, 66 to 1, 72 to 2, and 78 to 3, then wins/draws/losses and goals determine the table. In Formula One, teams are ranked each Matchday and receive configured position points—by default 25, 18, 15, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1—which accumulate in the championship table.

Set Maximum participants from 2 to 100. It limits accepted memberships and matters before initialization because every league member must have a Fantasy Team. Head-to-Head scheduling also needs the final set of participating teams.

Creation then asks for the initial roster rules. Initial budget defaults to 500 credits: each Fantasy Team starts with that remaining budget, purchase prices consume it, Market signings consume more, releases return the configured refund, and an enabled trade cash adjustment transfers credits. Credits have no external monetary value.

Set the release refund percentage from 0 to 100. Refunds use the recorded purchase price: a player bought for 40 with a 50% refund returns 20 credits on release. Set maximum squad size and separate goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, and forward limits; the combined role limits must be capable of supporting the maximum.

After creation, defaults are installed for formations, bench, substitutions, scoring, and Market/trades. You arrive in the new league as Commissioner, but creation does not allocate squads or initialize a championship. Invite managers, review all League Rules, create/assign Fantasy Teams, and record the agreed squads next.
creatingLeague.callout: The creator is the Commissioner. Choose the Season and league type carefully; competition initialization later locks important structural choices.

buildingSquads.title: Building the Initial Squads
buildingSquads.overview: Kaiser XI does not run an initial auction, sealed-bid contest, or draft. Organize that decision offline, then record its agreed outcome in Squad Setup.
details: Traditional auction: gather the managers, nominate one eligible player at a time, let the group bid, and record the winner and purchase value. Continue under whatever external nomination and tie rules your group agrees, then give the Commissioner the final team/player/price list. It is lively and makes the budget central, but requires everyone to attend and accurate bookkeeping.

Sealed bids: managers privately send bids to an agreed organizer by an external deadline. The highest valid bid wins; Kaiser XI does not receive the bids or break ties, so agree an external tie rule in advance. This method is flexible and private, but the organizer must reconcile simultaneous bids and budgets before entry.

Draft: agree a selection order and take turns choosing unassigned players. Each player can ultimately be active on only one Fantasy Team in the league. A draft can make bidding less central, but every recorded purchase price and final squad must still respect the Kaiser XI budget, overall size, and role limits.

Before entry, normalize the offline record: one owner per Fantasy Team, one team per player, a whole-number purchase price for every assignment, and totals within the initial budget. Confirm that each player is registered for the league’s selected Season and has the expected role.

Keep four concepts separate: the offline initial allocation decides who should own whom; Initial Squad Setup reproduces that agreement in Kaiser XI; the in-season Market signs free players and releases owned players during an open window; Trades exchange players between two existing Fantasy Teams.

None of the suggested offline methods adds hidden rules to Kaiser XI. Your group may choose its own nomination order, bid increments, tie-break, draft order, or timer, but Kaiser XI validates only the squad, role, uniqueness, price, and budget rules it actually stores.
buildingSquads.callout: Do not look for an Auction, Bids, or Draft button. Preserve the offline results and let the Commissioner enter them accurately.

leagueOverview.title: Understanding Your League
leagueOverview.overview: The league area combines a summary with navigation whose available destinations depend on league type, membership, ownership, and initialization state.
details: Start on the league summary to confirm the League name, description, selected competition/Season, type, status, capacity, and your role. Commissioners also see administrative controls that ordinary members do not.

Fantasy Teams lists the league’s teams and links to each detail page. A team page shows its owner, remaining budget, roster, player roles, purchase prices, and permitted management actions. A member needs an assigned team before submitting formations or proposing team-to-team trades.

League Rules shows the effective saved settings. Commissioners may edit settings while lifecycle and compatibility checks allow it; members can use the page as the definitive reference for this league.

Market lists Season-eligible players and whether they are free or assigned, plus signing, releasing, Market configuration, and trade proposals when those controls are available. The Market must be enabled, have both timestamps, and be inside its opening-inclusive/closing-exclusive window for roster transactions.

Matchdays lists the real Season rounds relevant to the initialized competition. Open one for its time window, formation link, calculation state, and—after calculation—team or fixture results and player detail.

Standings appears for initialized competition formats and reflects calculated results: cumulative fantasy points in Classic, match table records in Head-to-Head, or cumulative position points in Formula One. Head-to-Head also exposes its generated Calendar/fixtures; Classic and Formula One use championship Matchdays from the selected starting round onward.

If a destination or action is missing, first check initialization, whether you own a Fantasy Team, whether you are Commissioner, whether the Market is open, and whether the Matchday deadline has passed. Absence is often an intentional state or permission restriction.
leagueOverview.callout: Use this chapter as a map; later chapters describe each workflow and its validation in detail.

leagueRules.title: League Rules
leagueRules.overview: League Rules are the enforceable configuration for roster construction, formations, automatic substitutions, scoring, league-type conversion, and the transaction window.
details: Roster and money: initial budget seeds every new Fantasy Team; release refund percentage determines the purchase-price share returned on release; maximum roster players caps the squad; and four role limits cap goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders, and forwards. Existing squads prevent a Commissioner from lowering limits below their current contents, and initial budget cannot be rewritten once teams exist in an unsupported way.

Formation and bench: Allowed modules are selected from 3-4-3, 3-5-2, 4-3-3, 4-4-2, 4-5-1, 5-3-2, and 5-4-1 by default. Bench size is exact at submission, and role limits cap how many bench players of each role may be chosen.

Substitutions: Maximum substitutions cannot exceed bench size. Bench order tries playable reserves in the saved order; role priority moves same-role candidates ahead of others. If formation changes are disabled, every replacement must preserve the submitted module. If enabled, Kaiser XI may use another allowed module whose final role counts are valid.

Player scoring coefficients separately configure goals, assists, yellow cards, red cards, own goals, penalties scored, penalties missed, penalties saved, and goals conceded. Defaults are +3, +1, -0.5, -1, -2, +3, -3, +3, and -1 respectively. A penalty goal uses the penalty-scored value rather than receiving both penalty and ordinary-goal bonuses.

Optional scoring: Real-captain bonus adds its configured points to a contributing player marked captain of his real club. Goalkeeper clean-sheet bonus adds its value only to a contributing goalkeeper whose performance has clean sheet recorded. Neither switch changes the underlying base rating.

Defense modifier requires an effective, playable goalkeeper and at least four effective, playable defenders. Kaiser XI takes the three highest available defender base ratings, adds the goalkeeper base rating, averages those four ratings, then applies the bonus for the highest configured threshold reached. Event-adjusted fantasy scores are not used for this average.

Head-to-Head only: First goal threshold gives goal one; each complete goal interval above it adds another. With 66 and 6, 65.5 is 0, 66 is 1, 71.5 remains 1, and 72 is 2. Formula One only: the position-points map awards the configured non-increasing whole-number points after each Matchday ranking.

Market/trades: the Commissioner enables the Trade Market, sets opening and closing date-times, and chooses whether cash adjustments are allowed. The Market is closed unless all three availability conditions are satisfied. Trade proposals use the same window. Rules may be edited only by an authorized Commissioner and structural settings become locked or compatibility-limited as the league progresses.
leagueRules.callout: Review every section before entering squads and initializing. A displayed default is a real rule and will be enforced.

championship.title: Championship Configuration
championship.overview: Initialization freezes the participating Fantasy Teams and connects them to future Matchdays; league creation alone does not start competitive play.
details: Only a Commissioner can initialize. First ensure every accepted league member owns a Fantasy Team, there are at least two teams, and the desired starting Matchday belongs to the selected Season and has not started.

For Classic and Formula One, choose one future starting Matchday and initialize once. Kaiser XI records all current Fantasy Teams as championship participants; eligible championship rounds run from that starting Matchday through the remaining Season Matchdays.

For Head-to-Head, configure a future start, the number of round robins, and the leg order supported by the setup screen. Kaiser XI generates the round-robin Fantasy fixtures onto available Season Matchdays. The available future Matchdays must be sufficient for the requested schedule, and a schedule cannot be initialized twice.

Classic creates no pairwise fixtures: each participant’s calculated team score contributes directly to its cumulative championship total. Formula One also creates no pairwise fixtures: each included Matchday ranks participating teams and converts rank to configured position points. Head-to-Head creates the actual pairings used for match goals and table records.

Initialization is separate so the Commissioner can finish membership, teams, squads, and rules before making the competition structure official. A late member without a team blocks readiness, and teams added after the participant snapshot are not silently inserted.

After initialization, do not expect a reset button. The same competition cannot be initialized again, the start must stay in the future at initialization time, and lifecycle-protected structural settings can no longer be freely changed.

Checklist: all invitations resolved; every member has exactly the intended team; at least two teams; offline allocations entered and verified; budgets and role limits valid; scoring, lineup, Market, Head-to-Head thresholds, or Formula One points reviewed; correct future start selected; enough Matchdays available for a Head-to-Head schedule.
championship.callout: Initialization is a one-time structural action. Verify participants and the selected future Matchday before confirming.

squadSetup.title: Initial Squad Setup
squadSetup.overview: The Commissioner reproduces the offline allocation by creating/assigning Fantasy Teams and recording each player with the agreed purchase price.
details: Create the required Fantasy Teams and assign each to the correct current league member. Team names identify the competitors; ownership controls who can submit that team’s formations and use member transaction actions.

Open each Fantasy Team and add only players eligible for the league’s selected Season. Record the agreed whole-number purchase price. Kaiser XI marks the assignment active and deducts that price from the team’s remaining budget.

A player cannot be actively assigned to two Fantasy Teams in the same league. A signing also fails if the team lacks credits, has reached maximum roster size, or has reached that player’s goalkeeper/defender/midfielder/forward limit.

Use the role provided by the player’s active Season registration; it is not an arbitrary roster label. If an offline list names an unavailable player or a different role, reconcile it before proceeding rather than forcing an unsupported assignment.

Compare every team’s remaining budget with the offline ledger. With a 500-credit start and purchases totaling 430, 70 remains. Purchase values matter later because releases refund a percentage of that stored value, while trades preserve the exchanged players’ purchase values.

Before declaring setup complete, verify every accepted member has the correct team; every intended player appears once; names, roles, and prices match the record; no player remains on the wrong team; roster totals and per-role totals comply; and no budget is negative.

Initial setup records the starting state; it does not run the offline allocation and does not open the Market. Initialize the championship only after the participant/team readiness checks succeed and your group has reviewed the saved rules.
squadSetup.callout: Keep the offline allocation sheet beside you and verify one Fantasy Team at a time before initialization.

market.title: Market
market.overview: The Market is the in-season transaction area for Season-eligible free and assigned players; it is distinct from the offline initial allocation.
details: The Commissioner must enable the Trade Market and provide both opening and closing date-times. It is open at the opening instant and closes at the closing instant. Outside that interval—or if any configuration is missing—signings, releases, and trade actions are rejected.

Use the directory to search/filter eligible players and inspect assignment status. A free player has no active assignment in this league; an assigned player shows the Fantasy Team that owns him. Eligibility comes from an active registration in the league’s Season.

To sign, the owner of a Fantasy Team chooses a free player and enters a non-negative whole-number price. On success, the player is assigned, the price is saved, and the same number of credits is deducted. Example: a team with 35 credits signs for 12 and has 23 left.

A signing fails if the Market is closed, you do not own the acting team, the player is no longer free/eligible, the price is invalid, the budget is insufficient, the roster is full, or that role limit is reached. Refresh if another manager may have acted first.

To release, choose one of your active roster assignments and confirm. The assignment ends and the player becomes free. The refund is based on its stored purchase price and the league percentage; with price 40 and refund 50%, 20 credits return. Integer credits use the application’s rounded refund result.

A release can be rejected when the Market is closed, the assignment is no longer active or yours, or the action would conflict with current validation. Releasing can leave fewer players for a valid formation, so inspect the next Matchday lineup before confirming.

Market timestamps and cash-trade permission are Commissioner settings; ordinary managers cannot extend the window. Trades are proposals between already-owned players and are covered separately, although they require this same Market to be open.
market.callout: A listed player may cease to be available before confirmation. Successful server validation, not an old directory view, determines ownership.

fantasyTeam.title: Your Fantasy Team
fantasyTeam.overview: The Fantasy Team page is the durable squad record; a Matchday Formation is a separate, time-limited selection drawn from that active roster.
details: Confirm team name and owner first. Your ownership determines lineup and Market/trade permissions; contact the Commissioner if the wrong member is attached.

The budget summary shows remaining credits, not the original allowance or a prediction. Initial assignments and Market signings reduce it, qualifying releases refund it, and accepted cash-adjusted trades transfer it.

The roster lists active and, where presented, historical assignments with player identity, Season role, purchase price, assignment time, and release state. Purchase price is relevant for refund calculations and remains attached when players are exchanged in a trade.

Use available actions to update a permitted team name or, when the Market is open and you own the team, manage eligible roster transactions. Commissioner-only setup controls or actions belonging to another owner are not shown to ordinary members.

Your roster is a pool, not the automatic starting XI. For every eligible Matchday, open Formation and explicitly choose an allowed module, exactly eleven starters matching its roles, and the required ordered bench.

A player released after an earlier formation was submitted remains part of that historical submitted snapshot, but cannot be selected from the active roster for a new draft. Always review current roster totals before the deadline.
fantasyTeam.callout: Remaining budget buys flexibility, but only a complete role-balanced roster can produce a valid Matchday formation.

formation.title: Formation
formation.overview: A Formation is the saved and then submitted Matchday lineup. Build it before the Matchday starts; only a confirmed submission is used in calculation.
details: Open an eligible Matchday and its Formation for the Fantasy Team you own. The deadline is the Matchday start time. Before then you may build a draft; at or after it the editor is locked and late save/submit attempts are rejected.

Choose one module allowed by this League Rules page. The pitch shows the role structure—for example, 4-4-2 requires one goalkeeper, four defenders, four midfielders, and two forwards. Select exactly eleven active roster players matching every required role.

Select exactly the configured bench size without exceeding its per-role limits. A player cannot be both starter and reserve. Order the bench deliberately: position is used directly in bench-order mode and still resolves ties/order within substitution logic.

Save stores a valid draft for later editing but does not make it count. Submit validates the module, eleven starters, required role counts, exact bench, bench role limits, unique active roster assignments, ownership, Season eligibility, and deadline; success marks the Formation confirmed with a submission time.
After submission the Formation is read-only. Calculation ignores unsubmitted drafts. Check the submitted view rather than assuming that a successful earlier Save was a submission.

Module change safety: selecting the same module changes nothing. If starters exist and you choose a genuinely different module, Kaiser XI asks for confirmation. Confirming changes the module and clears all starters but preserves the bench; canceling leaves the entire draft untouched. Clearing is necessary because the new positional requirements could make the old XI invalid.

Automatic substitutions run only during result calculation. Each non-playing starter is considered in starter order. Kaiser XI tries playable unused bench players according to bench order or role priority, never exceeds maximum substitutions, and accepts a candidate only if the resulting eleven exactly matches the submitted module—or another allowed module when formation changes on substitution are enabled.

Example: in a submitted 4-4-2, one defender has no playable score. With a playable defender first on the bench and substitutions available, that defender enters. If only a midfielder is available and formation changes are disabled, nobody enters; the missing starter contributes nothing. If changes are enabled, the midfielder enters only when the resulting role counts match another allowed module.
formation.callout: Save is not Submit. Confirm the submitted state before the deadline, and treat bench order as a competitive decision.

matchdays.title: Matchdays
matchdays.overview: A Matchday connects one real competition round to formations, real performances, and the derived fantasy result.
details: The hierarchy is Real Competition → Season → Matchday → Real Matches → registered-player performances → Fantasy results. A league’s Season selection determines which branch of this hierarchy it can use.

Before a Matchday, the page shows its number and start/end times, eligibility in the initialized competition, and the Formation action when you own a participating team. Build and submit before starts_at; the start is the hard lineup deadline.

During the Matchday, submitted formations are locked while real matches and performance data are completed. Kaiser XI does not offer live lineup edits, and a partial data view should not be treated as a final fantasy result.
A PlayerScore becomes usable when its recorded status is playable and has the needed score data. Non-playing or pending records do not contribute and may trigger bench substitution resolution.

After the Matchday end, an authorized Commissioner can Calculate when the Matchday belongs to the initialized competition. Every participating team needs a confirmed submitted Formation for a complete set of team results; Head-to-Head fixtures also need both team scores.

After calculation, the Matchday exposes calculated team totals, detailed contributors and substitutions, and the format-specific results. Use previous Matchdays for historical submitted formations and published results rather than editing them.
matchdays.callout: The start time closes formations; the end time opens manual calculation. They serve different purposes.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.overview: Scoring proceeds from a recorded base rating and events to a player fantasy score, then sums the effective eleven and optional team bonuses.
details: Base rating is the source assessment of the real performance. Events are counts for goals, assists, yellow cards, red cards, own goals, penalties scored, penalties missed, penalties saved, and goals conceded; clean sheet and real-captain state are flags. Final fantasy score is base rating plus each event count multiplied by the League Rule coefficient.

Default coefficients are goal +3, assist +1, yellow -0.5, red -1, own goal -2, penalty scored +3, penalty missed -3, penalty saved +3, and goal conceded -1. A goal that is also recorded as a scored penalty receives the penalty value instead of an additional ordinary-goal value, preventing double counting.

Only effective, playable starters count: submitted starters who played plus valid automatic substitutes. A non-playing unresolved starter and unused bench player contribute zero. The Fantasy Team Matchday score is their player fantasy scores plus enabled real-captain, goalkeeper clean-sheet, and defense-modifier bonuses.

Real-captain bonus is awarded to every contributing performance marked as captain of the player’s real club, using the league’s configured value. Goalkeeper clean-sheet bonus requires the contributing player’s Formation role to be goalkeeper and clean sheet to be recorded; the switch and value must both be configured.

Defense modifier uses base ratings only. It requires one effective playable goalkeeper and at least four effective playable defenders. Take the three highest defender base ratings, combine them with the goalkeeper rating, divide by four, and apply the bonus at the highest configured threshold not above the average. Missing ratings or fewer qualifying players mean no modifier.

Complete example with default event coefficients: ten effective players have final fantasy scores totaling 60.0. The eleventh has base 6.5, one ordinary goal, one assist, and one yellow: 6.5 + 3 + 1 - 0.5 = 10.0, so base team points are 70.0. If that player is real captain with an enabled +0.5 bonus, the goalkeeper has an enabled +1 clean-sheet bonus, and defense base ratings 6.0, 6.5, 7.0 plus goalkeeper 6.5 average 6.5 and earn the default +2 threshold, the final team score is 73.5.

The stored PlayerScore may also contain a source final score, but league calculation applies the league’s current event coefficients to the recorded rating/events. Inspect the result breakdown to see which players counted and which optional bonuses were added.
scoring.callout: Always read the coefficients in your League Rules; the numerical example uses defaults and explicitly stated optional bonuses.

results.title: Results, Standings and Calendar
results.overview: Calculated Matchdays preserve the submitted lineup, effective substitutions, team score, and the competition-format interpretation of that score.
details: Open a calculated Matchday to see each Fantasy Team total and player breakdown. The historical Formation distinguishes original starters, bench players, substitutes actually used, the player replaced, non-contributors, and each counted player’s points.

Team totals separate base/player contribution from the goalkeeper clean-sheet bonus and defense modifier; real-captain points appear in the contributing player’s detail. This lets you reconcile the final number with Scoring and automatic substitutions.

Classic standings rank championship participants by cumulative calculated Fantasy Team points across included Matchdays. A Matchday score is not converted into a win or position award; it simply adds to the championship total.

Head-to-Head results convert each paired team’s fantasy points into goals using the League Rules. The result becomes win, draw, or loss. The table records played, wins, draws, losses, goals for/against, goal difference, and league points, with configured standings tie-break ordering applied by Kaiser XI.

Formula One ranks the Matchday’s calculated teams by fantasy score and then deterministic tie handling. Each position receives the configured position points, and the championship standings sum those awards across included Matchdays.

The Head-to-Head Calendar shows generated fixtures by round/Matchday and their result state. For Classic and Formula One, browse the championship Matchday list from the initialized starting round. Open an earlier round to inspect its immutable submitted Formation and last calculated result.
results.callout: The same team fantasy score has three different competitive meanings; always interpret it through the league type.

calculation.title: Calculate and Recalculate
calculation.overview: Calculate materializes derived fantasy results after a Matchday; using it again explicitly rebuilds those results from the current source data and rules.
details: Only an authorized Commissioner sees the action. It becomes available after the Matchday end, and only for a Matchday belonging to the initialized championship or generated Head-to-Head schedule.

Before Calculate, ensure participating teams submitted confirmed Formations and the relevant PlayerScores are complete/playable. Calculation resolves substitutions, computes every submitted team’s score and detail, builds Head-to-Head match results when applicable, refreshes the appropriate standings, and records the league/Matchday calculation time.

A missing submitted Formation prevents that team score from being created and can make a Head-to-Head fixture impossible to finalize. Invalid duplicate or incomplete source records also cause calculation to fail rather than fabricate points.

Already derived results do not silently follow later data corrections. Example: a player was recorded as 6.5 and the Matchday was calculated; the source is corrected to 7.0. The published fantasy result remains at the calculated value until the Commissioner deliberately calculates again using Recalculate.

Recalculate deletes that league’s existing derived Fantasy Match results and Team Matchday scores for the round inside one protected operation, then rebuilds team details, format-specific results, and standings using current PlayerScores and current effective League Rules. Source data and submitted Formations are not rewritten.
Use Recalculate only after a genuine correction to performance data or a supported rule correction that should affect history. Because standings may change, tell managers why it is being done.

If rebuilding encounters invalid/incomplete data, the operation fails and its transaction restores the prior derived result rather than leaving a half-rebuilt Matchday. Correct the underlying data or missing submission, then retry.
calculation.callout: Calculation is explicit and historical corrections are explicit. Kaiser XI does not silently rewrite calculated competition history.

transfers.title: Transfers and Trades
transfers.overview: Market sign/release actions move players between free status and one team; Trades exchange one owned player from each of two Fantasy Teams.
details: Both workflows require the League Market to be enabled and currently inside its opening/closing window. A member must own a Fantasy Team. Signing/releasing is described in Market; it is not called a Trade proposal.

To propose a Trade, choose another current Fantasy Team, one active player you offer, and one active player you request. The teams must differ, both players must still belong to the expected teams and be Season-eligible, and an identical pending proposal cannot already exist.

If cash adjustments are enabled, add a non-negative whole number of credits and identify which of the two teams pays. With zero cash, no payer is specified. The service does not permit cash when the setting is disabled.

The recipient can Accept or Reject a pending proposal; only the proposer can Cancel it. Accepting rechecks everything at that moment—the open window, pending/unexpired state, ownership, registrations, each resulting role limit, cash configuration, and payer budget—because rosters may have changed since proposal.

On acceptance, the two old assignments end, replacement assignments move the players while preserving their purchase prices, any cash moves between remaining budgets, and the proposal becomes accepted. Rejection or cancellation changes only proposal status and no roster/budget.
An expired proposal cannot be accepted, rejected, or cancelled through pending actions; it makes no roster change. Expiration is a time restriction on the proposal, not an automatic player exchange.

Example: Lions offer a defender bought for 20 to Eagles for a midfielder bought for 30, with Lions paying 5 credits. If cash is enabled, Lions have at least 5 credits, the Market is open, and both post-swap role counts are valid, acceptance exchanges the players, keeps their 20/30 purchase values, subtracts 5 from Lions, and adds 5 to Eagles.
transfers.callout: A proposal is not a reservation. Acceptance always validates current ownership, budget, role limits, expiry, and Market state again.

commissioner.title: Commissioner Guide
commissioner.overview: The Commissioner operates the league’s membership, enforced rules, recorded starting state, competition lifecycle, Market window, and explicit result calculation.
details: Create the league with the correct Season, type, name, description, capacity, budget, refund, and roster limits. Then inspect all default League Rules, including lineup, scoring, type-specific, and Market/trade settings.

Create invitations for managers and share their links securely. Monitor pending/accepted membership, capacity, and assigned league roles; ensure each accepted member receives the intended Fantasy Team before initialization.

Run the auction/bids/draft externally, create the Fantasy Teams, record every eligible player and purchase price, and reconcile remaining budgets, uniqueness, roster size, and role totals. Kaiser XI records rather than conducts this initial allocation.

Initialize only after readiness: every member has a team, at least two teams exist, the correct future Season Matchday is selected, and Head-to-Head has enough future rounds for its configured schedule. Initialization cannot simply be repeated.

Configure Market enablement, opening, closing, and cash-adjustment permission. During operation, the Commissioner does not need to manually approve valid member signings/releases/trades, but should communicate windows and avoid changing compatible rules unexpectedly.

For each Matchday, remind managers before the start deadline. Real match, registration, and PlayerScore administration is exposed to authorized back-office administrators rather than ordinary league members; Commissioners calculate only once the round has ended and data is ready.

Operational sequence: Create League → invite managers → configure rules → complete the external allocation → create/assign teams and enter squads → verify readiness → initialize championship/schedule → configure/open the Market → monitor Matchdays → Calculate → Recalculate only for communicated corrections.

Commissioner-only actions are protected even if a member knows the route. When a control is absent, verify Commissioner role, lifecycle, initialized state, required data, and relevant future/open time window before treating it as an error.
commissioner.callout: Use a checklist and communicate irreversible initialization, transaction windows, and every historical recalculation to all managers.

profile.title: Profile and Personalization
profile.overview: Account settings change your identity, sign-in security, language, and personal visual appearance without changing competition data.
details: Open Account to review the signed-in profile. Update the editable name and email fields and save; validation prevents an invalid address or one already used by another account.
Use the password form to change your password when needed. Enter the current password and the required new-password confirmation; this is separate from profile details.

Choose English, German, or Italian from the language selector. The choice changes supported interface and Game Instructions text for your browser; it does not translate user-entered League or Fantasy Team names.
Choose among the available football-inspired color palettes. They are visual themes only and do not claim affiliation with real football clubs.
Language and theme are personal preferences. Changing them does not alter League Rules, scoring, Market state, another user’s appearance, or any saved Matchday result.
If a preference appears unchanged, reload after confirming it was saved and verify you are using the same browser/account storage. Competition actions never depend on palette choice.
profile.callout: Personalization changes how Kaiser XI looks to you, not how your league works.

faq.title: FAQ and Troubleshooting
faq.overview: Most blocked actions follow a specific deadline, ownership, lifecycle, budget, eligibility, or roster validation. Use the messages and checks below before retrying.
details: Why can’t I submit my Formation? It must be before the Matchday start, belong to your team, use an allowed module, contain exactly eleven unique active starters with exact module roles, and contain the exact bench size within role limits. Save first if no Formation exists; then Submit and verify confirmed state.

Why did starters disappear after changing module? You confirmed a genuinely different module. Kaiser XI deliberately clears starters because their role counts may not fit; the bench stays. Canceling the dialog would have preserved the draft.
Why can’t I select this module? Only modules enabled in this league’s rules are offered. Ask the Commissioner before lifecycle locks, or choose an available module.

Why can’t I sign or release? The Market may be closed; you may not own the team; the player/assignment may have changed; a signing price may exceed budget; or size/role limits may be reached. Releases refund only after a valid active assignment is released.

Why is the Market unavailable? Enablement alone is insufficient: the Commissioner must set both times, current time must be at/after opening and strictly before closing, and your membership/team permissions must allow the action.

Why can’t I propose or accept a Trade? Check open Market, team ownership, different teams, active Season-eligible players, duplicate status, cash setting/payer/budget, resulting role limits, and that the proposal remains pending and unexpired. Only recipient accepts/rejects; only proposer cancels.
What happens when a Trade expires? It cannot be processed and exchanges nothing. Create a fresh valid proposal during an open Market if both managers still agree.

Why didn’t a corrected PlayerScore change a result, and when should Recalculate be used? Calculated history is a snapshot. After correcting 6.5 to 7.0, a Commissioner must explicitly Recalculate that completed initialized Matchday; use it only for real corrections because results and standings are rebuilt.

Why can’t the Commissioner initialize? Every accepted member needs a Fantasy Team, at least two teams are required, the start must be a future Matchday in the selected Season, initialization must not already exist, and Head-to-Head needs enough future Matchdays for its schedule.

What happens when a starter does not play? Calculation searches playable unused bench players in the configured order, within maximum substitutions, and accepts only a role/module-valid result. If none fits, the starter stays unresolved and contributes zero.

Why wasn’t a bench player used? He may lack a playable score, be behind another valid reserve, exceed maximum substitutions, or make the role counts invalid. Cross-role replacement requires formation changes on substitution and a resulting allowed module.

Why no defense modifier? You need the option enabled, an effective playable goalkeeper with a base rating, at least four effective playable defenders, and base ratings for the best three; their four-rating average must reach a configured threshold.

Why no goalkeeper clean-sheet bonus? The option must be enabled, the player must contribute as Formation goalkeeper, and the PlayerScore must explicitly record clean sheet. Merely conceding zero in a display is not a substitute for that recorded flag.
faq.callout: Do not work around a validation failure by guessing. Recheck the League Rules and current state; ask the Commissioner only for actions that are actually Commissioner-controlled.
